prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer induction–aircraft-loading handoff; airline loading excluded; no explicit modes.
Baggage Control System (Velvet) associates bag/passenger/flight records, validates routing, applies approved screening profiles; loads time-effective approved sort plans, checks current flight/handling records before routing. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight/routing records; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory (recipient unspecified). Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates conveyor readiness/restrictions/availability with plans; produces Recovery Route Card.
Staff verify eligibility, identity, flight, dimensions/weight; resolve missing/unreadable/conflicting data before induction. Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance; sends Oversize Exception Ticket; oversized bags require designated holding/staff-approved routing. Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable tags and Calibration Witness Tag when required. Transfer Bag Feeder records arrivals; sends Late Transfer Bag Card; holds pending screening/onward-handling confirmation.
Induction Tray Conveyor spaces bags for identification/imaging; jams/open doors/downstream unreadiness interlock feed. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner identify at route decisions, image, return dispositions; latter produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Incomplete examinations never clear. Image Resolution Desk staff review full images/identity/prompts, record dispositions; pending review bars make-up.
Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity, applies destination/screening status; sends Chute Occupancy Note near configured limit. Routes favor approved capacity/timing; blocked/unavailable chutes prohibit release. Bag Reconciliation Station matches identity/screening records before handling. Alarm/unresolved/missing-record bags require examination via Secondary Inspection Chute; access duty-authorized. Inspection staff retain alarmed bags until authorized disposition; isolation requires securing area/notifying Baggage Operations Supervisor. Normal return requires consistent identity/outcome/routing authorization.
East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor convey; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages only validly screened/authorized bags. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms readiness; Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance/sends Carousel Release Slip upon build authorization.
Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates flight-readiness/staffing/lane-operation/recovery with Security Duty Manager/Maintenance Technician. Escalated decisions notify Security Duty Manager; Explosives Response Team (Pebble) responds/coordinates safety with airport security personnel.

New part:
S088: A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
S089: Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
